title: streaming: improve client-cancel, disconnect/reconnect resume, and server-side timeouts
author: Aisha Malik
release_notes: Improved streaming lifecycle handling: client cancel processed server-side to free compute, reconnect/resume support for interrupted streams, and safer server-side timeouts with structured cancel reasons. No API breaking changes.
description:
Motivation: Customers running long-running streaming responses (LLM completions with tool calling, structured outputs, or long generations) see incorrect billing/compute hold when clients drop connections or explicitly cancel. This PR implements a set of lifecycle controls so that server compute is released quickly on client cancel, streams can be rejoined/resumed where possible, and server-side timeouts emit structured cancellation reasons for observability and client-side handling.

What I changed: consolidated streaming lifecycle control paths across the API gateway, runtime, and OpenAI-compat layer. Main features: 1) Client-cancel propagation - when the client issues an explicit cancel (HTTP/2 RST_STREAM, client-sent cancel message on WS/SSE), we now surface a cancel token to the runtime worker to interrupt decoding/kernels and close the KV/cache context immediately. Worker-level cancellation is cooperative: we added a short (50ms) preemption window to allow the runtime to emit a final partial event when safe. 2) Disconnect handling and reconnect/resume - streams now advertise a resume token (stream_id + last_token_index + signature). If a client reconnects within the configured resume_window (default 60s) and presents a valid resume token, we resume from the last committed token instead of restarting, preserving KV cache and avoiding duplicated compute. 3) Server-side safe timeouts - added two server timeouts: idle_stream_timeout (default 30s) for idle connections and request_compute_timeout (default 120s) for maximum compute time. On timeout we now emit a structured cancel event with cancel_reason set to one of ["client_cancel", "disconnect", "server_timeout", "compute_limit"] and include minimal resume metadata where applicable. 4) OpenAI compatibility layer updates - behavior aligned with common OpenAI streaming semantics: explicit 'done' events, cancel reason mapping, and resume-token header names (X-Redwood-Resume-Token / Redwood-Resume-Token). 5) Observability and metrics - added streaming.lifecycle.* counters and histograms: stream_cancelled, stream_resumed, stream_timeout_ms, resume_success_rate.

Files touched are kept limited to the API gateway, streaming runtime hooks, openai-compat adapter, and tests. No public API surface breaking changes; resume-token usage is opt-in via headers and opt-in config in Dedicated/Private.

Checklist:
- [x] Propagate client cancels to runtime workers
- [x] Add resume token generation & validation
- [x] Server-side timeout handling + structured cancel events
- [x] OpenAI-compat mapping for cancel/done semantics
- [x] Unit and integration tests
- [x] Performance canary + load-test on perf-canary

How to test: Unit tests added under runtime/streaming and api/gateway. Integration tests simulate HTTP/2 client RST, SSE disconnect, and reconnect with resume token. Manual load test run in perf-canary shows median tail latency unaffected and compute saved ~18% on simulated client cancels.

Rollout plan: feature gated behind flag runtime.streaming.lifecycle_v2. Default enabled in staging on rollout; gradual rollout to production (20% -> 50% -> 100%) with a canary perf run and monitoring of streaming.lifecycle.stream_timeout_ms and stream_resumed counters.

Compatibility notes: Existing clients that do not send resume tokens will continue to work (resumes won't be available). OpenAI-compat clients should get same 'done' behavior and cancel mappings. No change to request/response JSON shape except the structured cancel event (documented in release notes).

review_comments: Liam Chen: is the resume token signed? how do we rotate keys?

Aisha Malik: yes, tokens are HMAC-signed using the resume signing key stored in KMS. rotation is supported via a key-version header; fallback verification tries last 2 keys. documented in tooling/resume_token/signature.go
Sofia Patel: can the resume window be configured per-tenant? we had a customer ask for longer resume windows for mobile clients.
Aisha Malik: made resume_window tenant-configurable; default 60s but can be set in Dedicated/Private deployment configs. also exposed as runtime flag for hosted API
Ravi Kapoor: I saw one flaky integration test that failed due to race on committing last token index. please add a commit/ack handshake.
Aisha Malik: added commit handshake in runtime/worker/stream_context.go and updated tests. verified stability in local CI and canary runs.
Liam Chen: lgtm after minor nit about logging level for resumed streams (info->debug).
Sofia Patel: approved — matches ENG-1423 acceptance criteria.
